episode.title: Route macOS workspace launches through an encoded application deep link
episode.before: At parent commit 12c37a6b5cdb3fff2c03a355ca9948866bf1df07, the macOS launcher invoked `open -a <app_path> <workspace>`, passing the workspace as a macOS document-open argument. The resolution commit explains that recent desktop builds could focus the application without honoring that folder argument, so `codex app [PATH]` could fail to open the requested workspace.
episode.after: At commit f94c49cf465b7403f22894f2db1432dee66fd64e, the launcher converts the workspace path into the `path` query parameter of a `codex://threads/new` URL using form URL encoding, then passes that URL to `open -a <app_path>`. Its failure message reports the same URL handed to the operating system. A unit test parses a deep link built from a path containing a space and `#` and confirms that the scheme, host, route, and decoded query value preserve the intended workspace.
episode.diff: The single changed file, `codex-rs/cli/src/desktop_app/mac.rs`, adds `codex_new_thread_url`, which lossily converts the platform path to text, serializes it as a `path` query pair, and prefixes the query with `codex://threads/new?`. `open_codex_app` now constructs this URL and supplies it to the existing `open -a` subprocess instead of supplying the raw workspace path; the nonzero-exit diagnostic is updated accordingly. The same file adds `codex_new_thread_url_encodes_workspace_path`, covering URL parsing and query round-trip behavior for reserved characters. Existing upstream call sites still canonicalize the requested CLI path when possible and route both already-installed and newly-installed application launches through `open_codex_app`.

evidence_units.claim: Commit f94c49cf465b7403f22894f2db1432dee66fd64e is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 25485, has parent 12c37a6b5cdb3fff2c03a355ca9948866bf1df07, and changes only the macOS desktop launcher file.
evidence_units.source: `git show --format=fuller --stat f94c49cf465b7403f22894f2db1432dee66fd64e`; `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status -r f94c49cf465b7403f22894f2db1432dee66fd64e`; issue-bundle.json linked pull request and commit records

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, `open_codex_app` passed the workspace path directly as the final argument to `open -a`, and its error diagnostic described that raw-path invocation.
The change replaces the raw workspace argument with a generated URL in both the subprocess invocation and nonzero-exit diagnostic.
The added URL builder serializes the workspace under the `path` query key with `url::form_urlencoded::Serializer` and returns the explicit `codex://threads/new` application route.

Both the existing-application branch and the install-then-launch branch pass their resolved application path and the requested workspace to the same `open_codex_app` boundary, so the deep-link handoff applies in either launch path.

The CLI `app` command accepts a workspace path, canonicalizes it when possible, and forwards it to the platform desktop-app launcher; the behavioral change therefore covers the documented `codex app [PATH]` entry point without changing its input contract.

The added unit test builds a deep link from `/tmp/codex workspace/#1`, parses it as a URL, and asserts scheme `codex`, host `threads`, path `/new`, and a decoded `path` query value exactly equal to the original workspace string.

The resolution commit records the focused verification command `just test -p codex-cli codex_new_thread_url_encodes_workspace_path`. The available bundle does not include CI status or captured command output.
evidence_units.source: Commit message for f94c49cf465b7403f22894f2db1432dee66fd64e as recorded by `git show` and issue-bundle.json

evidence_units.claim: The stated failure was that macOS document-open delivery could focus the desktop application while failing to honor the supplied workspace; the explicit application-owned deep-link route remained supported.
evidence_units.source: Commit message sections `Why` and `What Changed` for f94c49cf465b7403f22894f2db1432dee66fd64e

candidate_atomics.name: encode-target-in-owned-deep-link
candidate_atomics.title: Encode the requested target in an application-owned deep link
candidate_atomics.description: Construct a URL for the destination application's explicit route and serialize the requested filesystem target as a query value so spaces, fragments, and other reserved characters retain their data meaning.

semantic_action.intent: Preserve the exact requested workspace while expressing the launch request through the destination application's supported navigation contract.
semantic_action.pre_state: A workspace path is available, and the destination application exposes an explicit URL route that accepts that path as a query parameter.
semantic_action.post_state: A parseable application deep link identifies the new-workspace route and decodes its target query value to the original workspace text.
semantic_action.validation: Parse a generated link for a workspace containing reserved characters and assert the expected scheme, authority, route, and decoded query pair.

candidate_atomics.name: handoff-owned-link-to-application-launcher
candidate_atomics.title: Hand the application-owned link to the operating-system launcher
candidate_atomics.description: Replace a fragile document-open target with the encoded application deep link while preserving application selection, launch-status handling, and useful failure diagnostics.

semantic_action.intent: Make launching or focusing the desktop application also deliver the requested workspace through the application's explicit routing surface.
semantic_action.pre_state: The launcher selects an application bundle but supplies the workspace as a document-open argument that the receiving application may ignore.
semantic_action.post_state: The launcher selects the same application bundle and supplies the generated deep link as its handoff argument; failures identify the actual link used.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the subprocess argument construction to confirm the generated link replaces the raw path, then exercise both upstream launch branches or a command-level spy to confirm they converge on this handoff and retain nonzero-status failure propagation.
parameters: application_path: selected or newly installed application bundle

candidate_workflows.name: replace-fragile-document-open-with-owned-deep-link
candidate_workflows.title: Replace an unreliable document-open handoff with an explicit application route
candidate_workflows.description: When an operating-system application launcher opens or focuses the correct application but loses the requested target, encode that target in a supported application-owned deep link and pass the link through the existing launch boundary.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure a CLI request to open a workspace reaches the selected desktop application with the exact target intact, including paths containing URL-reserved characters.
when_to_use: The operating-system launcher successfully selects or focuses the destination application but its generic document-open argument is not reliably honored.
The destination application provides a supported deep-link route capable of representing the requested target.
The target must survive transport through URL syntax without spaces, fragment markers, or other reserved characters changing its meaning.
anti_goals: Do not redesign application discovery, installation, architecture detection, or download behavior.
Do not shell-escape or concatenate the workspace into a URL manually when a structured query serializer is available.
Do not change the CLI workspace argument contract or optimize unrelated installer behavior.
Do not treat successful process launch alone as proof that the target was encoded or delivered correctly.
not_applicable_when: The destination application has no supported deep-link contract for the requested operation.
The failure is application discovery or process startup rather than loss of the target during handoff.
The target cannot be represented by the receiving application's textual URL contract without an explicitly accepted lossy conversion.
The platform launcher cannot pass URLs to the selected application.
inputs: Requested workspace path from the CLI entry point
Supported application deep-link scheme, authority, route, and query-key contract
Operating-system application-launch command and exit status
workflow_graph.entry_state: The CLI has resolved a workspace and an application bundle, but the launch boundary passes the workspace as a generic document argument that may be ignored by the receiving application.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All existing application-launch branches hand a parseable, correctly encoded application-owned route to the platform launcher, and encoding tests prove that representative reserved characters round-trip to the original workspace value.

steps.condition: The receiving application exposes an explicit deep-link route for opening the requested target.
steps.validation: Parse the generated URL and verify its routing components and decoded target query value, including a path with a space and `#`.

steps.condition: The platform application launcher accepts the deep link as the application-open argument.
steps.validation: Confirm the launcher receives the generated link rather than the raw filesystem path, both pre-existing and newly-installed application branches reach this boundary, and nonzero exit status still produces an error containing the actual handoff target.

validation_ladder: Unit-test structured URL construction by parsing the result and asserting scheme, authority, route, and decoded query pairs.
Use a target containing URL-reserved characters to prove query serialization preserves target identity.
Inspect or spy on the operating-system command invocation to prove the encoded link, not the raw path, is handed off.
Exercise both the already-installed and install-then-launch call paths because both must converge on the corrected handoff.
On a supported platform with the desktop application available, run an end-to-end CLI launch and confirm the requested workspace is opened, not merely that the application is focused.
stop_conditions: Stop if the receiving application does not document or support an explicit route for the requested target.
Stop if URL parsing or query decoding does not reproduce the intended target.
Stop if any launch branch bypasses the corrected handoff boundary.
Stop if process success cannot be distinguished from successful target delivery; retain end-to-end validation as unresolved rather than claiming it.
unresolved_or_deferred: No CI status, review discussion, or captured output from the recorded focused test command is present in the evidence bundle.
The checkout and bundle establish URL construction and command wiring, but do not provide an automated assertion over the spawned `open` command arguments.
Actual end-to-end behavior in a recent macOS desktop build is not demonstrated by the available unit test.
The path conversion uses `to_string_lossy`; behavior for non-Unicode filesystem paths is not specified or tested by this change.

unresolved_questions: Did CI or a local run of `just test -p codex-cli codex_new_thread_url_encodes_workspace_path` pass? The commit records the command, but the supplied evidence contains no execution result.
Was the corrected launch verified end-to-end against an affected macOS desktop build, confirming that the requested workspace opens rather than only the application focusing?
Is lossy conversion of non-Unicode workspace paths an accepted part of the deep-link contract?
